At the same time, the other side of my flat facing the Mojmilo waterworks was risky, too. So my children slept in the bathroom or in the hall, which wasn't really that safe in itself. But the rooms that I had just specified were the riskiest of all.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And you started talking about 1992. Did the situation in 1994 and 1995 change in that respect, in relation to safety in your apartment?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: Yes. There was considerable improvement. UNPROFOR arrived at the airport, so that side was now safe. And then the Serb soldiers left the waterworks later on, so that side became safe, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: In general, in 1994, summer 1994, 1995, were there places you would consider being safe in Dobrinja, or was there no such place?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: It wasn't safe.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Let me turn to the incident at the Simone Bolivar school in June 1995 when there was shelling. Do you remember that incident, Witness?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: Quite well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Was there a member of your family who ventured out to get water on the 18th of June, 1995?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: It was me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And do you recall the weather on that day?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: I think it was a lovely day.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And why did you go to the water-pump on that day?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: Well, quite simply, I heard that water would be distributed and I wanted to give my husband a hand, because until that time he had been the only one fetching water for us. And the school was nearby, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: How did you get water? Did you have canisters?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: Yes, 5-litre jerrycans. We would tie them up in pairs so we would be able to carry two at a time. We would use a length of rope or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: On that morning, on the 18th of June, 1995, did you have those jerrycans with you when you walked from your home towards the school?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: No. We had been told the previous day or two days before, I'm not quite certain, that we would be getting some water. Those of us living in nearby buildings left our jerrycans there, in a queue, as it were. So as soon as they told us to go and fetch water, we would be right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And between the time you left your jerrycan at the school and the 18th of June, when you actually went to get water, was there shelling?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: Yes. Probably my memory is a bit blurred. But, yes, until they started giving us water -- or the day before, rather.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Was there a limit of water every person could take with him or her from the water-pump back home?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, it was per household, 20 litres, I think, I'm not sure. At first they said 40 litres, but then there were too many of us and they wanted to get the whole thing over with. And then they said they would be allowing 20 litres per household.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters's note: Could all other microphones please be turned off when the witness is speaking. There is too much background noise interfering with the witness's voice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I hope that was heard by all the parties. All the microphones are to be turned off when the witness is speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, I think it's primarily directed at me, Mr. President. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Witness, were there other people waiting, like you were waiting, for water on that day?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And how many people were there?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: I think there were over 50 of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And can you describe these persons waiting for you? Were they men, women, children?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: More women and children, but there were some men as well. There were people there I didn't even know, I only got to know them then, some people who lived in the same building as I. So they were familiar.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Were there soldiers among these people waiting, or policemen?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: No. Policemen kept telling us that we shouldn't all go in a large group to that open area. They said we should go one by one.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: But on that day did you see policemen, you know, being around, or were these policemen not there on that day?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: We had been warned not to go on that day. I'm not sure who it was, some civilians or something, but they told us not to go to that clearing, to that open area, all together in a single group.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Who operated the pump?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: I really don't know. One thing I do know is Mr. Muharem, who was wounded, too, would carry the pump back home. He was probably put in charge by someone, or, rather, from civilian protection. So he would then bring the pump back to that spot. And we would stand at our windows or word would reach us one way or another that water would be distributed. But it wasn't really that often.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, was there an explosion then, on that morning, at the Simone Bolivar school?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And where were you when the explosion occurred?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: I was in the school building, the one that had been destroyed. I was near a door and was waiting for a gentleman who had gone on before me to fetch water. I was waiting for my turn to go and get water and that's when he heard the explosion.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Mr. President, Mr. Registrar, if ter number 00119 could be called up, and it's been admitted, at least parts of it, as P257 and marked by a previous witness. But I would like to show a few photographs to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And while it's being called up, how far away from the pump were you, Witness, when the explosion occurred?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: The distance was smaller than the distance between me and that door over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And were you closest to the pump, or were other people between you and the pump?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: There were people who were in the process of fetching water, who were using the pump, who were closer than I was. I was waiting for my turn.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: If you can have a look at this photograph. Witness, do you recognise the photograph?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's the school building. After the shelling, it had burned down, as you can see. It's the Simone Bolivar school. And it was a hollow shell, so to speak. In the middle of that building, there was a skylight. They probably grew flowers there once upon a time. This was considered to be the safest water-pump in Dobrinja, because all the other ones were outdoors, in open areas, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: If we can move - yes, thank you very much - to the next picture on the same page, just a little bit lower.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Do you recognise this picture, Witness?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is the opening in which I stood. Right there. I'm not sure if I should point it out. Do you want me to?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, please, if you could take a pen, which will be handed to you by Ms. Usher, and mark with an A the location where you were standing the moment the explosion occurred.

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: This is where I was standing. Right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And can you indicate to Their Honours the water-pump, if you can see it, and mark it with a B.

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And I see that there are empty canisters there. Did you have similar canisters like those ones, or perhaps did one of them even belong to you and your family?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: I think not. I didn't make it to the pump, not before it happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Maybe one last question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: If we can go back to the first -- well, first let me ask to have it tendered, this photo. Perhaps -- Mr. President, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Witness, can you use this photo and tell us where the other people were waiting to get water, the people who were even behind you when the explosion occurred, and if you can mark it with a C.

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: Right behind this wall, and over there, too. And of course there were several people around the pump itself; maybe five or six.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Mr. President, I apologise, if these photos -- this photo can be tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P285, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Witness, did you get injured?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And what were your injuries?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: The upper leg, the flesh, not the bone; and I received another injury to the heel of that same leg, which is my right leg.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And did you see other people injured or killed?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: At the time this happened, yes, I did see some people who were injured, and I saw some people who were dead by the time I reached the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Can you tell Their Honours the names of people who were injured and killed?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: I can tell you the names of those I knew. Resad Imamovic, a neighbour of mine; Kenan Cizmic, a 19-year-old man, my daughter's school mate; and a total of seven others who were killed. Eleven or 12, were wounded. As for those wounded, I knew Kalabic Afan. The rest I knew by sight, but I didn't know their names.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And these two people whom you saw killed, Mr. Imamovic and Mr. Cizmic, did you see them alive the same morning?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: So they died there on the spot as a cause of this explosion?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: Resad Imamovic was killed on the spot --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think this is a leading question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: "So they died there on the spot as a cause of this explosion." Yes, it's leading, and you must avoid that, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Do you know how come these people, whom you saw alive in the morning, are now dead around lunch-time? Do you know the reason for that?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: The explosion.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. I'd like to show you another Prosecution exhibit, that is, ter number 00113.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And again, Mr. President, Your Honours, it's been admitted by a previous witness as Exhibit P259.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Prosecutor, you wish to move on to another document, do you? May I just ask a question. Witness, on the 28th of June, on this spot, seven people were killed and 11 people injured, after the explosion; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 18th of June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I have understood you correctly, in your statement you say that there was an attack on the 17th -- the 16th and the 17th, so I would like to put to you the following question: Can we understand this explosion to be part of the assault or attack of one army -- one army attacking another, or would this be a deliberate attack on this particular location?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It appears that it was a deliberate attack. The morning itself it had been quite peaceful. As for previous days, one thing I have to say is that Dobrinja was shelled on a regular basis; the whole of Sarajevo, for that matter. But I myself was living in Dobrinja and that's all that I can testify to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My last question: Had this pump already been targeted? Had there been injured and killed people before the 18th of June?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: If ter number 00113 could be shown, please. I'm interested in the second page. Perhaps the B/C/S version could also be moved to the second page. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, Witness, towards the bottom of that page, you see a number of people listed as killed. Do you see the two persons you had mentioned before, Mr. Kalabic and Mr. Imamovic, listed there?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: No. Cizmic -- Kalabic was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that clarification. And Mr. Imamovic?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: Yes. Imamovic and Cizmic were the two who were killed. Those were the two I knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. And if we go to the bottom of the English version - and I think it might be on the next page in the B/C/S version - the list of wounded people on that day, do you see your name?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: Yes. Number 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And does the information stated there reflect the injuries you had on that day?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And I believe you said that Mr. Afan Kalabic was also injured, that you know him. Do you see his name mentioned here?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And do the injuries attributed to him also reflect your knowledge, what you saw at that time?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi, we're going to take the break now, but is that your examination, or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: It's about five or ten more minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No. We'll take the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Witness, just a couple of more questions and then I'm done, from my side. You described your injuries. Did somebody take care of your injuries?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: Yes, the staff at the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And which hospital was that?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: Dobrinja Hospital. It used to be an outpatient clinic, but it was transformed into a full-fledged hospital during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And how far away was it from the Simone Bolivar school?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: There was the building in which I lived between the two, and I can point that out for you, if you like.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I have asked for the bird's-eye view, ter number 2981, to be displayed, and I would like Madam Usher to assist the witness so she can make an A for the Simone Bolivar school.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: If you recognise that school.

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. And then can you mark your apartment.

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And can you please put the letter B beside the cross you just made.

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No need to apologise. And, lastly -- a couple of more questions. Can you point the way or the path you took on the morning when you went from your apartment to the water-pump? And please also indicate with a letter C where the water-pump was located.

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: This is the skylight, where it used to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And can you indicate the way you were walking along from your apartment to where you were waiting to get water from the pump.

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: Just a minute, please. There is something I'd like to say, if I may. This building that we see in the photograph is the new school. I realise now that it has been mended. I'm not sure if the skylight is still in the same spot as it used to be. I don't know. But I do know that this wall was destroyed. So this is where the old one might be and where they kept the position of the old one. I can't say with certainty, but the skylight was nearby, and the water-pump, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Can you mark, please, where you thought the wall from the old school building was with a marking.

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: You mean the one that was destroyed?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: Which letter shall I put?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: D.

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. And incidentally, the water-pump, was it covered, was it in a room, or was it open air?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: That was the safest pump in Dobrinja, as I said a minute ago. The pump itself was below what used to be the skylight and glass which was destroyed in the war, and one could see the sky through this open area.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, before the break you indicated that there was a barrier erected against snipers in the street behind the Simone Bolivar school. Can you also make a marking and also attach to it the letter E where these sniper protection devices were?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: Approximately here. In order to cross the street behind the school, facing this neighbourhood were garbage containers, and people were running there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: The witness just marked something that appears to be the letter E above the letter A.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And, lastly, in relation to this photo, can you tell us where the hospital was to which you were taken?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: What letter shall I put?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I'd suggest F.

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: I don't know if it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Is that accurate or is that approximate?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: Approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, if we could move on to the next --

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, if we could tender that exhibit into evidence. I'm grateful to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P286, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I'm grateful to Ms. Bosnjakovic. The next image I would like to show is ter number 02986, please. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise this photo?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's the school playground between my building and the school; however, this fence was erected after the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. And can you just indicate your apartment with the letter A, please.

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: I cannot see it from here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And can you give an approximate direction where the apartment was?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'll try. I think somewhere here. You said letter A?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: Approximately here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, lastly --

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: -- I would like you to have a look at a map.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And, Mr. President, unfortunately we have to go back to the stone age and use the ELMO. While doing that, if this exhibit here could be tendered, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P287, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I believe there are hard copies for you as well. It's simply an enlargement of the usual map we are always using with these witnesses. It's a blown-up version.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Witness, can you please indicate using a pen - and I think for this matter you have to use another pen, a conventional one - the Simone Bolivar school. Yes. Make a circle around it.

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And please attach the letter A to the left of it.

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you. And if you can also mark your apartment with a little circle and attach the letter B to it, please.

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: This is the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. And, lastly, these sniper barriers you mentioned and you marked on the photo, where were they located?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: How shall I mark them?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Just a line. And please add the letter C on the right side to it.

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And perhaps if you can see that, can you tell Their Honours where the airport is on this map?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Can you make a circle around the words.

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And please attach the letter D to it.

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: If this exhibit could be tendered, please, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P288, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: My last question, Mr. President, is:

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Witness, can you very, very briefly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Witness, can you very briefly tell Their Honours what happened to your mother during the war.

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: My mother was captured in Kula and kept in detention for about 80 or 90 days, simply because she went to visit my sister who fled from Grbavica to Hrasno. My mother didn't know her way around this neighbourhood. She went to Grbavica and she was taken to Kula. We failed to release her through the Red Cross and in all other ways. But we failed and she remained there for 90 days, and she was 83 years old.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. That concludes my examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Isailovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Witness. I am Branislava Isailovic, member of the Paris Bar Association. I'm the counsel of General Milosevic before this Chamber. I would like to ask a few questions on your evidence. First of all, I would like you to give us a word of explanation on something.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But perhaps for this purpose, we'd need to have on the screen the picture P285, 285, already tendered by the Prosecutor. Should it be my assistant doing this, or not?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: We were talking about this well or this pump which was located inside that Simone Bolivar school. We'll see the picture. But first of all I'd like to ask you whether it was a well on which the pump was installed, or were these normal public facilities with drains and pipes, pipes bringing the water? Do you know that, or not?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but I assume that these pumps were installed whenever there was need for water in Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: At that time it would happen that you had water in your apartment.

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: Yes. Sometimes we had water.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll ask the interpreters to translate the answer again.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Because earlier on you said "pustala se voda."

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: Yes. Water supply was restored for a couple of hours. I can't tell you exactly at what intervals. Sometimes it happened that there was no water for months, in a row, and then we would get some water for a couple of hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, at the time, do you know who was in charge of the water supply?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, the Serbian forces were holding the waterworks.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: You thought it was the Serbs who were in charge and who were controlling the water?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: Yes. Otherwise, we would have had water, had it not been the case. We would have had regular water supply.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And you can see the picture and you can see here the device, the pump. In your statement and in your evidence today, you said that it was a Muharem who was actually keeping this device in his place. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: This upper part of the pump that can you see is portable. In order to prevent people coming there whenever they felt like doing so, he took it with him to his home. Whenever water was available, he would bring this pump and install it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you said that this Muharem was a member of the civil protection; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. Possibly, judging by his age. I really don't know, madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And on that day --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What was his age?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I couldn't tell you. He was an elderly person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: A few days before the 18th of June incident, you said that -- you said Muharem would not install the pump because of lack of security.

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: As far as you know, was it Muharem making decisions on whether the situation was suitable for installing the pump, or was it someone else?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: I believe it was the civilian protection; that's why I mentioned the civilian protection. I believe that they were the ones who allowed or disallowed water to be fetched.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Coming back to my first question, do you think that the water was pumped from a well which was bored underneath the school?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, this water was found there, but this water was not drinking water.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: To make sure I understand you, the water for which you were queueing was industrial water; it was not drinking water.

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: Yes. We didn't drink this water; we just used it for washing laundry.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And how did you manage for drinking water? And which kind of water did you use to cook?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: From the well, or if the supply were restored after months, then we would collect as much as we could.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And where were the wells located for this drinking water?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: I never went to this well. My husband did. I'm not very knowledgeable about estimating distances, but I would say approximately 500 metres from my house.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And possibly you also learned from your husband in which neighbourhood these wells were, where you used to go.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: If you look at the map that you have on the ELMO, can you see C5 on that map?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: This is C5 neighbourhood and this is approximately the distance, diagonally. So, roughly speaking, it was closer to C5. And I think that this neighbourhood is called Aerodromsko neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, did you know who at the time was in control of what there in Dobrinja? For example, C5 was under the control of which army?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: It was a free territory and we could move freely.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: You've just shown the airport area. Can you point to this again, point to the airport area. Do you know who was -- under the control of whom this area was?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: The Serbian army.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We may have a technical problem because we only have one copy marked by the witness. Can we tender this? It may be useful to have the marking we've just made now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Well, so far the witness hasn't made an additional marking. She can certainly use a red pen to make additional markings. I also have another copy which can be used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Well, let's proceed on that basis.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With a red pen, then, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you mark this as C5. This would be the well, the well with drinking water. Can you just mark it with the letter C and figure 5.

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: One had to pass through C5 neighbourhood in order to reach this area, so approximately between Aerodromsko neighbourhood and C5. I can't show you exactly here on this map because I can't read a map properly.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Could you just circle the area where you believe it to be, which you described a while ago. You said it was between the airport and a place neighbouring the airport. Could you circle the area roughly, the --

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: This area.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: It doesn't have to be too precise. And could you just mark this with the letter P, P standing for well, "puits."

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: We also mentioned the area controlled by the Republika Srpska, the area in the airport. If you could circle this on the map also, please.

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: This whole neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, Your Honour, I don't remember the number, but I think this is a P exhibit. So does this exhibit remain as it stands, or what are we to do? Do we keep the same number, in other words, for this exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We keep the same number.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you mentioned, and you said in your statement, the day before or perhaps two days before, you placed your empty jerrycans inside the Simone Bolivar school. Is this true?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And the day you went there, on the morning of the 18th of June, 1995, did you find your jerrycans in the same spot, as you'd left them?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: Approximately in the same place. And we all put our initials on our jerrycans.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And you didn't notice anything, that the jerrycans had fallen on the ground or that something had happened in that particular spot?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: No, no. They could have overturned because they were empty, but I didn't see anything unusual.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: I think I need to say something here. What I heard in my translation headset wasn't right. Were these jerrycans on the floor or not?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: They could have been overturned. Some remained, maybe, upright; some were overturned on the ground, because they were empty.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember a statement you made on the 23rd of February, 1996, which you gave the OTP? We're going to have it coming up on the screen so that you can be quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a 65 ter document, number 2980.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Now you can see the cover page, the first page, of your statement. Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: I can't see your signature. Can you see your signature?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: I can see it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to ask my case manager to go to page 3. This is the first paragraph I'm interested in, and in the English version, it's the second paragraph. So the first paragraph for the witness and the second paragraph for the English speakers in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Here you mention the presence of the police on that morning in that particular place; is that right?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: They warned us not to go there as a group, into an open space where the pump was. And I believe it was the police or the civilian protection who gave us this warning; I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: When you went there, when you went to the school, when you went inside, you saw the police, a policeman, did you?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: As I was approaching -- inside the room, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And here you say that it seemed strange. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure where I said that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, this is not word for word what you said. You said usually the police was not there.

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: I found it strange, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So this seemed strange to you, did it?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure if that was exactly what I said. But this man who brought the water-pump warned us, too. He would bring it whenever it was safe, and he would always say it as well. He would warn us to go one by one and not in a group.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: According to what you remember, could you tell us why the police were there on that day, which was rather unusual?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender your statement into evidence because the Prosecutor has not done so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D88, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Could we go back to the school now. This is what was left of the school, in other words. And around the square where the pump was located, the remaining walls of the school, were they around this area?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, in your opinion, the group of people inside the school walls, could they be seen from the outside, do you think?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: That depends on where you were looking from. If you were looking from the side where the wall had been destroyed, in that case the answer is yes. But not from the direction of the water-pump.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not quite happy with what I heard so I will put my question again. You're saying that you could be seen from your building; in other words, if someone was inside the building, he could have seen you, he or she could have seen you.

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: No, because that was deeper down, the entrance; the length of a rather sizeable room, if you like. But the wall had been destroyed and you could see that there were people inside.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And from the other sides, could you be seen or not?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: Me personally?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: No. I had the group of people inside in mind.

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: From the direction of the water-pump, one could only see me, because I was standing at what used to be the door, and the other -- the remaining people, the group, were behind that wall.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you talked about your unfortunate neighbour who was wounded and killed during that incident. Did you only see this person in hospital? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: We were standing in a triangle, the three of us. They were a little ahead of me, in what used to be the corridor of the school, and I was standing in the doorway. To my right was the one who was killed, and to my left, the one who was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And after the impact of the shell, did you still see these people?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: No. My eyes went blind at that moment so I didn't see those people. When I was rising to my feet, I did see people around me.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters could not hear the last part of the answer on account of the amount of background noise interfering with the witness's voice. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: May I ask you, Madam Witness, to repeat the last part of your question, as the interpreter did not hear it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You asked if I was able to see -- could you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: My question was: At the time of the impact, did you see them? Your neighbours, I mean, who fell.

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: Well, we had been talking just moments before. We were standing in some sort of triangle. So when this happened everything went black before my eyes. I fell down, and of course at that precise moment I didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, could we have the map of Sarajevo, showing the streets of Sarajevo, 65 ter document 2872, if this could come up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, this is a tourist map and we can see the streets of Sarajevo on it. It's going to take a while.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to ask the court officer or the usher, I don't know, to show us the left-hand side of the map which lies to the bottom of the map. If we could enlarge it somewhat, please. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see it properly? Can you find your way around on the map, Witness?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: I see it clearly, but I'm not very good with these maps.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps we could enlarge it a little bit more, the area where you can see the airport. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: That's better now, isn't it? Can you see the Dobrinja area now, your area? Perhaps the usher could help you and give you the electronic pen, please. Can you find your street, or your neighbourhood, rather, Dobrinja, and mark with the letter A, the place where your street is.

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: It's very small so I can only mark it roughly. I'm trying to make out something that is familiar. The letter A, you said? I'm not sure, but I think that's where it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Now, could you draw a circle around the airport and the runway, please.

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: I really can't see it. I think it should be marked, but I can't see it. It should be around here. Believe me, I can't see it. Hereabouts, roughly speaking.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, as you lived in this area, do you know where Mojmilo is on this map?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: I was living in this area, but Mojmilo is over here. I'm not sure if I marked it properly. Did I?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: What you have indicated to us is where Mojmilo, the area, is. But did you know the hill that was called Mojmilo?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: Not before the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: How about now? On the map, can you locate it?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Could you show us where it is. Could you mark it, please.

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: Should I use a letter?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Just circle it; it's not a dot. So just circle the area and mark with an M.

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: Just what I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Could you see Mount Mojmilo from your flat?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And what did this look like?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: What do you mean? What exactly do you mean when you say that?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: What does this mountain look like today? How high is it? Is it green? What does it look like?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: It isn't really that high. It's very green. Not that big, really, but quite long. It runs virtually the entire length of this street. It's like a long ridge but not very high, and quite green. I'm not sure if that's helpful. Is it?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is a help, thank you. When it was wartime, did you know that there was a tunnel under the runway, and the entrance to that tunnel was in Dobrinja and the exit was in Donji Kotorac? Does that ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: I know that the entrance was in Dobrinja. I don't know where the exit was, but you're probably right. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, at the time do you know where that tunnel led to?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: Well, probably Donji Kotorac. At least that's what you said. I'm not sure what you mean, really.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: I used the word "destination." Did you know where it led to? What I mean is --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Do you mean purpose, perhaps, purpose of the tunnel, or where did it lead to; interpreter's note.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: What was the purpose of this tunnel?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: People, many people, used it to get food.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Isailovic, I'm not able to ascertain where your cross-examination is leading.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did put the question to the witness because I wanted to know whether she knew of a tunnel that had been dug under the airport, under one of the runways of the airport, and she said she did know. So the next question had to do with the purpose of this tunnel, what purpose did it serve, and she said she didn't know. So I have no further questions on the existence of the tunnel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, the territory which was to the left, what I mean is the Dobrinja area, is that where the confrontation line between the two armies was located?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understand the question. Anyway, I didn't know where the lines were held by either army. I knew the approximate location of the Serbian army, but I wouldn't quite be able to put my finger on it now.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know that if one goes beyond the runway of the airport there's Butmir and Kotorac. At the time did you know who was controlling these territories?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: Yes. The BH army.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Just one last question, Witness. Did you see soldiers of the ABiH army in your area?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Any re-examination, Mr. Waespi?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, just very briefly. If the ELMO can be lowered so I can see the witness, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Witness, just two or three questions. The first one: You were asked to mark on the map where you thought that well was, and I think you marked it with a letter P, past C5 and just before that settlement you called Aerodromsko. You also said that your husband used to go there. Did you ever yourself go to that well?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Next question is: Was it a secret or was it a well-known fact that there was a water-pump installed at times at the Simone Bolivar school?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: Most of the time it was a secret because we couldn't tell when that would be, when they would bring water. There were no set times, if that's what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And you said that you had to cross the open area between your apartment and the Simone Bolivar school; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: The playground, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And I believe you also said it was a dangerous spot; that you had to cross swiftly. Do you remember that as well?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And can you remind us again why it was a dangerous spot, to cross between your apartment over the playground to the school?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: There was a sniper covering the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Madam Witness, this sniper area, do you know where that was? Can you tell us if the sniper nest, as it were, was that in -- who controlled the area where the sniper nest was?

utterances.speaker: AZRA SISIC
utterances.text: I'm not really familiar with the place, but the assumption was that this was above Nedzarici and that this was being held by the Serb army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Mr. President, just a clarification. I'm not sure whether the transcript captured the area. The witness indicated that it was the assumption that it was from which side?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Above Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Is it Dzarici or --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, that concludes your evidence. Thank you for giving it. You may now leave. We'll adjourn until tomorrow at 2.15 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 28th day of February, 2007, at 2.15 p.m. 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.56 p.m.,
